- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) mid-period, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 18-day history shows strong trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.5–0.8), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% ahead of true outcome for first 5–7 days.
- If 30-day forecast shows persistent downward trend despite positive sentiment, reduce downward bias by 0.5–1.0% for next 7–14 days.
